ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.33 voucher refund to the rider (RydeTAXI metered-fare overcharge), and remind the driver that unexplained off-route mileage is a breach of the shortest-and-most-direct obligation.
ruling.reasoning:
RD-1: the trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres enter the fare directly; the GPS record shows one unexplained off-route segment 09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, +3.07 km and up to 688 m off the optimal route [F3], and no exemption applies, so the segment is refundable under RD-2 [F3][RD-1].

RD-4: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F13]; the only congestion evidence is speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12], which is outside RD-4(b)'s band 1–2, and band evidence is corroborative only (G3). With no RD-4(a) incident the segment falls to RD-2 treatment [F11][F12][F13][RD-4].

RD-5: the driver's post-trip statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is not rider consent and, appearing only in his own statement, cannot exempt the segment (G11) [F10]. The chat is complete and timestamped: a 09:04 rider pickup note and a 09:05 driver "2 min away," with no route discussion before the segment started at 09:24 [F7][F8][F9]; the trace timestamps the segment start at 09:24:50, so no rider message sent before 09:24:50 agrees to anything. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment counts; the trace also notes no stop was measured, so RD-3 gives no exemption either [F3][F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

Amount (RD-2): the refund is the unexempted segment's extra kilometres priced at this trip's own per-km rate, which the fare record supplies as distance fare ÷ distance km = $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.41008/km [F6]. $1.41008/km × 3.07 km (extra_km in [F3]) = $4.3290, rounded to $4.33. The billed excess line of 3.20 km is a separate figure covering the whole-trip excess; RD-2 refunds only the segment's extra_km and expressly does not refund mileage outside any segment, so the award is computed from [F3], not from the 3.20 km in [F4] [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

RD-6: the driver's 90-day profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so the "repeated" route-deviation predicate is absent and no flag_account attaches; the profile facts (F15, F16) carry neither side's finding [F15][F16][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment 09:24–09:30 (+3.07 km, up to 688 m off the optimal route) is unexempted: the chat is complete and contains only a 09:04 rider pickup note and a 09:05 driver '2 min away', so no rider message before the 09:24:50 segment start agrees to any route change, and the driver's post-trip 'the GPS rerouted' is his own statement, not consent (G11). It is also not a rider-named stop, as no stop was measured in the segment. Refundable under RD-2 at the trip's per-km rate [F3][F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-3][RD-5][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The $4.51 in [F4] prices 3.20 km of whole-trip excess; RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km (3.07 km per [F3]) at the trip rate ($34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.41008/km [F6]), giving $4.33, and expressly does not refund mileage outside any segment [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

Its premise that the refund should be measured by the billed excess is wrong: RD-2 measures the unexempted segment's extra_km, so 3.07 km at $1.41008/km, not the 3.20 km whole-trip figure [F1][F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

Accepted; the prior 90-day upheld dispute is a no-show matter with route count 0 [F16], so RD-6's repeated-route-deviation predicate is absent and no flag_account attaches — the claim is upheld and therefore not a ground against this ruling [F16][RD-6].

Accepted on the safety screen: the chat and statement contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10], so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation does not trigger; this is a finding, not a defence to the refund [F7][F8][F10].

The rider's and driver's profile histories [F15][F16] do not decide the merits and are not used to establish the deviation; the finding rests on [F3] and [F6], and no flag_account arises under RD-6 [F15][F16][RD-6].

The whole-trip totals (+3.2 km, +15%; +8.4 min) [F1][F2] are not themselves refundable: RD-2 refunds only mileage attributed to an unexempted off-route segment, which here is 3.07 km, not the full 3.2 km [F1][F2][F3][RD-2].

what_would_change: F3: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $4.33 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
